SEDIMENT HYDROMECHANICAL PROPERTIES AND FERTILITY: IMPLICATIONS FOR SUSTAINABLE WATERSHED MANAGEMENT

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Arifjanov A, Samiev L, Allayorova L, Zakirov B, Donoboyev J, Seytimbetov A, Jovliev U.

ABSTRACT

This work is devoted to the study of granulometric, hydrochemical and agrochemical characteristics of river sediments deposited in the Kokand settling basin of the Sokh River system. The research takes into account the double role of these sediments, their potential as a natural source of nutrients to improve soil fertility and their impact on hydraulic performance. Laboratory analyses and field work characterized sediment particle size distribution and chemical composition. Correlation and regression analysis was also applied to study the relationships between sediment fractions and contents of nutrients. The results indicate that the settling basin is capable of retaining most of the fine particles, particularly silt and clay, with a retention efficiency of over 85-90%, and therefore it is an effective natural sediment separator. Medium-sized sand grains, on the other hand, travel with relatively little lag across the basin. Statistical analysis revealed a negative correlation between particle size and nutrient content, suggesting that the finer sediment fractions contained the more of the essential plant nutrients, especially potassium and phosphorus. The hydrochemical data indicate that the sediments are non-saline and conform to the FAO guidelines for agriculture use. These results show the importance of sediment fractionation in the spreading of nutrient-rich materials which can increase soil production and in the improvement of hydraulic operation in irrigation systems. Based on these results, the study provides useful recommendations for sustainable sediment management in semi-arid settings, through a comprehensive framework that links soil fertility, irrigation efficiency and sediment properties.
